author: Rui Carvalho
title: False landing gear warning caused by moisture in the sensor connector
description:
What happens: after washing the aircraft or heavy rain, a landing gear fault warning appears. It comes and goes, and the sensor is not faulty.

What I found: water and some early corrosion in the electrical connector of the left main gear sensor.

Fix: disconnect the connector, dry it with air, clean it with the approved contact cleaner and seal the connector again. Check the gap between the sensor and its target. Finally, run the system test on the on-board computer.

This avoids replacing the sensor and the landing gear computer, saving 4 to 5 hours of aircraft downtime.

author: Ana Ferreira
part: Valve linking the left and right fuel tanks (crossfeed)
alarm: Fuel valve light stays dim and does not go out
title: Fuel valve light stays on: check the switch before replacing the valve
description:
What happens: the pilot selects the valve linking the fuel tanks to closed, but the light stays dim, as if the valve were still moving.

Most common cause: the valve closes properly, but the small switch that reports it as closed is out of adjustment.

Fix: visually confirm the valve is closed, check the switch with a multimeter and adjust it. The video shows where to measure and how to avoid damaging the connector.

This avoids replacing a valve that is working.

author: Miguel Santos
part: Thin tube that measures engine bleed air pressure
alarm: Engine 1 bleed fault warning (ENG 1 BLEED FAULT)
title: Engine bleed warning right after start: cracked tube that only opens when cold
description: Voice note transcript: "Hi guys. We've had a bleed fault warning on engine one three times, always right after start-up, with the aircraft cold. They'd already replaced the system computer, and it didn't fix it. The tip is to check the thin pressure-sensing tube first, next to the valve. It has a crack that only opens when the tube is cold. That's why, when you test it with the engine hot, everything looks fine. With soapy water, and the engine at idle, you see the leak straight away. We replaced the tube and the problem never came back."

We replaced the tube and the problem never came back.

author: Joana Lopes
alarm: Engine running hotter than normal on take-off
title: Borescope inspection of the turbine blades: probe position that saves an hour
description:
When the engine starts running hotter than normal, we have to look at the turbine blades from the inside with a thin camera (borescope). It usually takes a long time because of the access.

Tip: go in through the right inspection port with the camera tip bent, and turn the engine by hand with the proper tool. That way you see the leading edge of the blades without moving the camera.

The video shows the sequence and how to tell normal wear from burn damage that means the engine has to come off.

author: Pedro Almeida
alarm: Air conditioning pack 2 overheat warning (PACK 2 OVHT)
title: Air conditioning overheats on the ground in summer: clean the heat exchanger before replacing sensors
description:
What happens: in summer, with the aircraft on the ground, air conditioning pack 2 gives an overheat warning.

The photo shows the air conditioning heat exchanger and the air inlet clogged with dirt and pollen. The sensor was fine.

Fix: inspect the air inlet and the heat exchanger, clean them and make sure the inlet door opens properly. Only then think about replacing sensors.

author: Carla Nunes
title: Error E-402 on the brakes: sensor wire worn by rubbing on a clamp
description:
What happens: the system that stops the wheels locking under braking switches off and error E-402 shows for wheel 3. It happens now and then while taxiing.

Cause: the sensor wire was rubbing on a clamp and the insulation was worn. The photo marks the exact spot.

Fix: repair the wire, refit the clamp in the right position with its spacer and run the system test.

author: Miguel Santos
alarm: APU shuts down by itself on low oil pressure
title: APU shuts down by itself: check the oil filter before replacing the sensor
description: Voice note transcript: "Right, about the APU, the small engine in the tail. If it shuts down by itself on low oil pressure, and the oil level is fine, the first thing to check is the oil filter. The clogged-filter indicator doesn't always pop out. We pulled the filter, and it was full of carbon particles. Replace the filter, check the magnetic plug for metal particles, and only then start thinking about the sensor."
transcript: Right, about the APU, the small engine in the tail. If it shuts down by itself on low oil pressure, and the oil level is fine, the first thing to check is the oil filter. The clogged-filter indicator doesn't always pop out. We pulled the filter, and it was full of carbon particles. Replace the filter, check the magnetic plug for metal particles, and only then start thinking about the sensor.

author: Tiago Ribeiro
alarm: Generator 1 not powering the bus (IDG 1 OFF BUS)
title: Engine 1 generator not working after an engine change: loose connector
description:
After an engine change, the generator on that engine did not come online on the first start.

The generator output connector was fitted, but not torqued correctly, and one terminal showed signs of overheating. I torqued it to the value in the manual, cleaned the terminal and the generator came online.

Suggestion: add this check to the engine change task list.

author: Sofia Martins
alarm: Low pressure warning on the centre tank pump
title: Centre pump warning with an almost empty tank is normal: check before replacing
description: Voice note transcript: "Hi everyone, a quick note. We've had several low-pressure warnings on the centre tank fuel pump, in flight. In almost every case, the tank was nearly empty, and the pump hadn't switched itself off yet. Before opening the tank, check the fuel quantity and the history on the on-board computer. It saves you a big job."
transcript: Hi everyone, a quick note. We've had several low-pressure warnings on the centre tank fuel pump, in flight. In almost every case, the tank was nearly empty, and the pump hadn't switched itself off yet. Before opening the tank, check the fuel quantity and the history on the on-board computer. It saves you a big job.

author: Bruno Teixeira
alarm: Hydraulic system B pressure loss warning
title: System B hydraulic pressure drops while parked: low nitrogen in the accumulator
description:
What happens: after the pumps are switched off, hydraulic system B pressure drops faster than normal, with no visible leak.

The video shows how to check the nitrogen pre-charge of the accumulator (a bottle that stores pressure) with the system depressurised. It was low on nitrogen. We recharged it and the problem went away.

author: Tiago Ribeiro
title: GPS failure solved by resetting the system
description: I switched the circuit breaker off and on again and the warning went away.
rejectReason: Resetting does not fix the root cause. Add what you checked (connector, cable and antenna seal) before resubmitting.
